claims.claim: The term out of doors was used in eighteenth-century North America to describe colonists and postrevolutionary citizens acting outside formal legal representative institutions.
claims.supporting_excerpt: In eighteenth-century North America, the term “out of doors” was frequently used to characterize the people of the British colonies, and then of the postrevoutionary United States, acting “outside of the legal representative institutions” by which they were governed, sometimes in mobs and crowds and sometimes through “extralegal associations.”

must_not_be_lost: The historical meaning and figurative use of the term out of doors in eighteenth-century North America.
